title: Capcom confirms data breach affecting 11.7 million accounts
content_md: Japanese gaming giant Capcom has confirmed that hackers breached its membership service, CAPCOM ID, exposing more than 11.7 million customer email addresses and associated information. Apart from emails, exposed data includes account creation date, last login timestamp, number of logins, and the IP address used at the last login. Capcom found that for a small subset of 43 accounts, dates of birth, gender, nicknames, and countries were also exposed. For another subset of 196 accounts, the hackers changed the CAPCOM ID login passwords in an attempt to lock the owners out, but the company took action and reset them. In an alert today , the gaming company says that passwords for all other registered members have not been exposed and that credit card information remained unaffected. Capcom is a Japanese video game developer and publisher known for franchises such as Resident Evil, Monster Hunter, Street Fighter, and Mega Man. The company has 4,000 employees and an annual revenue of $1.24 billion. CAPCOM ID is the company’s shared account system used for accessing its web services and playing some of its online games. Although the timing of the breach remains unclear, Capcom said it detected suspicious activity and confirmed unauthorized access on October 19. An investigation was launched immediately, and by the following day, it was clear that customer information had been compromised. October 21, the company reported the incident to the police and to Japan’s Personal Information
